id.title: Id
id.description: A short name, unique in this file, never changed once set.
id.$comment: Opaque: unique within this file, never parsed or rewritten. Real instances use github:…, did:…, exampledao:role:… and bare slugs. Identity across instances goes through handles.

name.title: Name
name.description: What the person, agent or organisation is called.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: A person, an agent, an organisation or a role. Left empty, a person.
kind.$comment: Absent or null reads as person, and so does `type: individual`, as some instances write it. Agents (crew seats) are kind agent.

role.title: Role
role.description: What they do here, in a few words.

layer.title: Layer
layer.description: How close they are to the core of the work.
layer.$comment: Open vocabulary. The framework's default words are the examples; an instance may use its own (dao-global, network, funders…).

left.title: Left
left.description: When they left, if they have.

email.title: Email
email.description: An address to reach them. Commits made with it are recognised as theirs.
email.$comment: Read as handles.email, and as a handles.git candidate (the vault hub writes it here).

handles.title: Handles
handles.description: How they are recognised: the emails their commits are made with (git) and their accounts (address).
handles.$comment: How an actor is recognised. git: the emails commits are made with (one or a list); address: CAIP-10 accounts (one or a list).

$comment: Optional fields accept null: in these YAML registries an explicitly-unset field is written as `null`, and refusing it made real entries unsavable.
